items.prompt: What is the primary difference between class attributes and instance attributes in Python?
items.title: Understanding Class and Instance Attributes
items.content: Class attributes are shared across all instances of a class and defined within the class but outside any method. Instance attributes are unique to each instance and defined within methods (typically __init__). For example, a class attribute like 'species' in a Dog class would be shared by all Dog objects, while an instance attribute like 'name' would vary per object.

items.prompt: Which of the following correctly identifies a class attribute vs an instance attribute?
options: A. Class attributes are unique to each instance; instance attributes are shared across all instances
B. Class attributes are defined inside methods; instance attributes are defined inside the class body
C. Class attributes are accessed via the class name; instance attributes are accessed via instance objects
D. Class attributes require initialization in __init__; instance attributes are automatically created
items.explanation: Class attributes are shared across all instances and accessed via the class name (e.g., ClassName.attribute), while instance attributes are unique to each object and accessed via the instance (e.g., obj.attribute).
